Welcome to the University of Calgary!
The University of Calgary is a world-class university that inspires and supports discovery, creativity and innovation across all disciplines. In addition to working with some of the best minds in your field, you will have access to workshops and services dedicated to your academic and professional development, ensuring that you have the best student experience possible. And you get to live in Canada's most enterprising city!
If you are thinking of working with an agent, please note that only applications made through the official UCalgary web application will be considered for admission. If successful, an offer will be sent directly to you from the university and made available in the Student Centre. The university does not release admission information to third parties, including agents. To accept your admission, you will need to log in to the Student Centre with an eID, a personalized unique ID for electronic access.
Before you apply
To be considered for admission to your graduate program, you must meet the admission requirements set out by the Faculty of Graduate Studies and by your graduate program of interest.
Understanding graduate studies
University of Calgary graduate students:
Get to live in the most livable city in North America
With a ranking based on stability, healthcare, education, infrastructure, culture and environment, Calgary is an incredible place to learn.
Have access to Alberta Health and the GSA health and dental plan
You’re eligible for a free provincial plan to cover basic services, and opted-in to cover many additional expenses through the Graduate Students' Association.
May be eligible for a 1-3 year post-graduate work permit
With the most head offices per capita in Canada, Calgary is a hub for innovation, leadership, and growth.
Represent over 140 countries globally
We respect human rights, value the voices and perspectives of all students, and foster a community of change-makers.
Study Permits and Provincial Attestation Letters
We encourage you to apply for a study permit as soon as possible after accepting your offer of admission. For best results, international students intending to study at University of Calgary beginning in Fall 2026 should submit their study permit application before May 1, 2026. You can check the average current processing times for study permits on the IRCC website.
Provincial Attestation Letters
As of January 1, 2026, graduate students joining master’s and doctoral programs will no longer require a Provincial Attestation Letter (PAL) to apply for a study permit. PALs will still be provided for international students joining an in-person graduate certificate or graduate diploma program.
Learn more about PALs

English language proficiency (ELP) score reporting
The Faculty of Graduate Studies sets minimum requirements for ELP in the Academic Calendar. Please note that some graduate programs have ELP requirements that are higher than the minimum requirements set by the Faculty of Graduate Studies. English Language Proficiency (ELP) scores must be received directly from the test score agency. We are unable to accept test results sent directly from applicants.
Below are common tests and how to report your score to the University of Calgary. To see all the available ELP requirement fulfillment options, see the Graduate Calendar.
Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL iBT) or the TOEFL iBT Home Edition
And obtaining a score of at least 86 (or 4.5 for tests taken after January 21, 2026)* (with no section less than 20 (minimum 4.0 in reading, writing and speaking sections; minimum 4.5 in listening section for tests taken after January 21, 2026)*).
When requesting that official test results are forwarded to the University of Calgary, indicate the institution code 0813 and the code appropriate to the graduate program, as listed on the TOEFL website.
International English Language Testing System (IELTS)
Instructions for sharing your score can be found on their website
The University of Calgary institution code is 139719
Pearson Test of English (PTE)
Instructions for sharing your score can be found on their website
Duolingo English Test
Instructions for sharing your score can be found on their website
To avoid delayed processing times please refrain from sending application documents before submitting your application.
English language proficiency (ELP) exemptions
A Graduate Program Director may exempt an applicant whose first language is not English from the ELP requirement if they meet the following criteria:
The student has completed
a Bachelor’s Degree (minimum of 3 years in length), or
a Graduate Degree
in an institution where the language of instruction and examination is English. If the institution has multiple languages of instruction, the Graduate Program Director may ask for confirmation of the language of instruction for your degree.
Eligible institutions must be listed as providing English language instruction in the World Higher Education Database (WHED). Please remember, even if you have a degree from an institution included on this list, exemption from ELP requirements remain at the discretion of Graduate Program Directors.

The University of Calgary, located in the heart of Southern Alberta, both acknowledges and pays tribute
to the traditional territories of the peoples of Treaty 7, which include the Blackfoot Confederacy
(comprised of the Siksika, the Piikani, and the Kainai First Nations), the Tsuut’ina First Nation,
and the Stoney Nakoda (including Chiniki, Bearspaw, and Goodstoney First Nations). The city of Calgary
is also home to the Métis Nation within Alberta (including Nose Hill Métis District 5 and Elbow Métis
District 6).
The University of Calgary is situated on land Northwest of where the Bow River meets the Elbow River,
a site traditionally known as Moh’kins’tsis to the Blackfoot, Wîchîspa to the Stoney Nakoda, and
Guts’ists’i to the Tsuut’ina. On this land and in this place we strive to learn together, walk
together, and grow together “in a good way.”
